text:
A simpler way
to order food
The problem we wanted to solve
Ordering food should feel clear from the first click to the final delivery update.
Customers often jump between menus, categories, and unclear restaurant information.
After placing an order, customers need a clear status and expected delivery time.
Wrong images, stale sessions, and confusing errors make a simple order feel risky.
Restaurant staff and administrators need one place to receive and manage orders.
QuickBite focuses the experience around one trusted restaurant catalog.
A focused set of goals guided the build.
A clean home page and category-led menu.
Validated prices, quantities, addresses, and payments.
ETA, status steps, partner details, and order history.
Owner and admin views for incoming orders and platform control.
The stack keeps the project familiar, modular, and easy to extend.
Document database for users, restaurants, menu items, and orders.
REST API routes, validation, authentication, and error handling.
Responsive customer, owner, and admin interfaces.
Backend runtime connecting the API, database, and business logic.
Vite  ·  JWT  ·  Mongoose  ·  Tailwind CSS  ·  Render  ·  MongoDB Atlas
The customer, operations team, and database meet through one API layer.
The important parts are visible in the flow, not hidden in the code.
Browse categories, filter veg or non-veg, and sort by price or name.
Dish-specific images, descriptions, prices, and availability.
Quantity controls, coupons, addresses, tax, and payment choice.
Live status steps, ETA, delivery partner, and review after delivery.
Owner receives incoming orders. Admin can monitor platform orders.
The same flow works on desktop and mobile screens.
Each major user action maps to a small, testable API surface.
The interface keeps restaurant identity and ordering context visible.
Rating and delivery time stay easy to scan.
The restaurant name and cuisine anchor the menu.
The full app continues the journey through menu, cart, checkout, and order tracking.
The build became stronger by fixing the details customers notice first.
Keeping menu images matched to names
Preventing stale tokens from breaking orders
Protecting server-side totals and status changes
Analytics for menu and order trends

A complete food ordering flow,
from menu to doorstep.
The project combines a focused customer experience with practical restaurant and admin operations.
